items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: And it influenced me quite a bit because I saw the beauty, you know.

ctx.x: Now, that was a club called the Radio Inn, I believe it was on 18th Street, and it was an after hours spot, and so on and so on. But I remember a guy came in one night who was there obviously with a show. He was a black guy, and his name was Putney Dandridge. This man made a tremendous impression upon me because he played piano and he had such beautiful bass lines. I had never heard this before.

Now, this guy -- I don't know, I haven't heard too much of him -- and I'm sure that there's a history, you know, a record of him, someplace. Putney Dandridge. But this guy had the most beautiful bass line on piano and it fascinated me. I never forgot it. And it influenced me quite a bit because I saw the beauty, you know. My mother always tried to tell me this, but here was a guy and I saw it with someone else. And he was a tremendous pianist. You see, but now the writers and the players now are very aware of…
